patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition, compulsive behaviors, and personality change in a previously reserved school principal.
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. V. is a 62-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman referred by her son for progressive personality changes over 2 years. He reports that his mother, formerly a reserved and professional school principal known for her decorum, began making inappropriate remarks at school board meetings approximately 2 years ago. She was eventually asked to retire early. Over the past year, her behavior has escalated markedly. She makes crude sexual jokes to strangers, has been found shoplifting small items (which she denies), and has made repeated unwanted advances toward a neighbor. She has developed compulsive behavior around food — she will eat continuously and has started eating food off other people's plates without permission. She also has a new compulsion to arrange objects in her kitchen in precise patterns for hours. Her son has found evidence of online gambling, spending over $8,000 in six months. She expresses no concern about any of this, stating she is 'finally doing what she wants.' She complains of no depressive symptoms, hallucinations, or pain. Neurological review of systems otherwise negative.

mri.impression: Severe bilateral (right-predominant) orbitofrontal and anterior temporal atrophy with knife-blade pattern on coronal T1 sequences. Normal hippocampal volume. Posterior parietal and occipital cortex preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Severe hypometabolism involving prefrontal and orbitofrontal regions

advanced_imaging.impression: Severe bilateral (right-predominant) frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex and parietal metabolism preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Amyloid negative — no significant uptake above threshold

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. Global SUVR 0.96, below positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 128 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 40 mg/dL. Glucose: 58 mg/dL (ratio 0.66). Abeta42: 845 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 198 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 35 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 1,988 pg/mL (elevated).

findings.result: Severely impaired — FAB 11/18; Trails B: failed; WCST perseverations: severe
Severely impaired — Faux Pas: 4/20; theory of mind: failed

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile consistent with probable behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. Severely impaired executive function (FAB 11/18, Trails B failed, WCST perseverations severe) and social cognition (Faux Pas 4/20, theory of mind failed) with retrieval-predominant memory pattern. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia management pharmacological nonpharmacological

results.title: Pharmacological management of bvFTD
results.finding: SSRIs (sertraline, fluvoxamine) may reduce compulsive and disinhibited behaviors; limited RCT evidence

results.title: Trazodone in FTD
results.finding: Trazodone 100-300mg/day reduces agitation and improves sleep in FTD (Lebert et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004)

results.title: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors in FTD
results.finding: No benefit demonstrated; may worsen behavioral symptoms due to acetylcholinergic-serotonergic imbalance

output.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia. SSRIs (sertraline, fluvoxamine) have modest evidence for reducing compulsive and disinhibited behaviors; evidence is largely from small trials and open-label studies. Trazodone has randomized controlled trial evidence for reducing agitation and improving sleep (Lebert et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004). Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors have not demonstrated benefit and may worsen behavioral symptoms. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions: Levothyroxine + sertraline: monitor thyroid function as SSRIs may alter thyroid hormone metabolism
warnings: Monitor for SSRI-associated hyponatremia in elderly female patients
alternatives: Trazodone 50-100mg at bedtime for agitation and sleep
